why: The owner, 2026-10-18: rename Vani's user-facing 'jev' naming to the model it runs, d1-ultra, with a read-side alias for existing ledger rows. Vani names the OpenRouter Decisions backend after its model slug (liquid/d1-ultra -> 'd1-ultra'); new ledger rows carry triage.<slot>.backend = 'd1-ultra'.
what_changes: Only the primary's backend name. The model (liquid/d1-ultra), its criteria and its LLM fallback are unchanged, and so is every field of the shadow under test (name 'local', prompt variant, criteria, fixture, reading rule, attempts, timeout, server, model).

shadow_config.name: local
shadow_config.reading_rule: no cut-off, no abstain path (decide/jev/jev.go readSlot): a choice among the options reads answered with p = confidence if present else probabilities[choice]; a missing or unknown choice, or p outside [0,1] or NaN, reads failed

primary.llm_fallback: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 (refused at check time: missing workspace ID)

shadow_config_hash_rule: Amendment 1's rule, unchanged: sha256 of JSON.stringify(shadow_config) with the key order above (node, no whitespace). Checked at drafting: the same computation over amendment 1's shadow_config reproduces 77d0f316443ace098d2334635a8874f1b1639cf1064200256da4d69a60dc0e8f.

diff_from_amendment_1.unchanged: Every other field of shadow_config is byte-identical to amendment 1, including key order (top level: name, prompt_variant, criteria, fixture_sha256, reading_rule, max_attempts, timeout_s, server, model, primary; primary: backend, model, criteria, llm_fallback).

hash_chain: Amendment 1 and its hash stay in the registration as history and are not edited. The verdict run's ledger row cites this amendment's hash, c850d9c3a3e1c1a7b3e5d5b98d6eec36a38b076ffc0ebd805a43d9b884adfa84.

legacy_rows_and_alias.rule: Ledger rows written before the rename carry the primary as 'jev'. Vani's readers (vani eval, vani label and the drop rule) read a primary backend of 'jev' as the configured OpenRouter decider's name. The alias applies only to the primary's triage.<slot>.backend and triage.backend fields, never to triage.<slot>.shadow_backend. Rows whose backend is 'llm', 'lappi', 'local' or empty are read as written.
legacy_rows_and_alias.evidence_at_drafting: Vani/.state/state/ledger/events.jsonl: 382 rows carry triage.role_fit.backend 'jev', and all 382 have triage.role_fit.shadow_backend 'local'. 382 rows have shadow_backend 'local' in all. No row has shadow_backend 'jev'. So no d1-3B reading was filed under 'jev', and the alias cannot credit a shadow reading to the primary. 300 rows carry backend 'llm' and 300 carry an empty backend; the alias leaves them alone. Counted by the drafting session; first counted by the 'Scope an on-device decider runtime' session.
legacy_rows_and_alias.equivalence: vani eval's numbers must not change because of the rename. Vani ships a test that runs eval over a fixture mixing 'jev' and 'd1-ultra' primary rows and checks that the result matches the same fixture with every primary named 'd1-ultra'. The same test asserts that shadow_backend and the 'llm' and empty-backend rows are untouched.
legacy_rows_and_alias.offline_script: held_out_computation in amendment 1 still applies. Any offline script that computes the held-out verdict must apply this same alias, and must first reproduce vani eval's all-labels numbers exactly.

deployment: The rename and the alias are deployed before the verdict run, and neither changes during it. That keeps the primary unchanged for the run, as what.primary requires.
directive_wording: In the owner's directive ('port d1 natively to tessl if it beats Jev'), 'Jev' now reads as 'd1-ultra, the backend formerly named jev'. The directive's condition is: the local d1-3B shadow beats the d1-ultra primary.
spend_key: Outside the registration. Vani keeps the daily budget file and its spend key as 'jev' (state/budget/jev.json), so the rename does not reset the day's spend cap.
